qt: to the Commission Kostas Papadakis (NI) Subject:

In Uzbekistan, the journalist Aziz Hakimov was sentenced to four years and two months in prison for ‘incitement to hatred’ because he took a stand against a bill promoting a ban on communist ideology and against the rehabilitation of participants in the Islamist armed movement of 1920-1940, which is guilty of a series of crimes against the peoples of Central Asia. In Azerbaijan, four young people were sentenced to prison simply for displaying communist symbols. Ibrahim Asadli and Abdulla Ibrahimli were each sentenced to two years in prison and Elçin Bayramlı and Mehman Zeynalov each received 18-month terms. They received these sentences simply for publicly displaying Soviet flags. This is a judicial practice that is being promoted in member states of the Organisation of Turkic States and is unacceptable, also when one considers that journalists in Kazakhstan are being prosecuted based on similar charges because they oppose the falsification of history. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Where does it stand on the unacceptable violation of civil rights and freedoms in Member States of the Organisation of Turkic States, with which the EU is in fact strengthening its economic, diplomatic and military ties?

What does it intend to do to secure the release of political prisoners in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan and stop the political persecution of communists and other activists who defend the USSR and the historical truth?
